saints.name: St. Faustina Kowalska
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: A humble Polish sister and “secretary” of Divine Mercy, to whom Christ entrusted the message of his boundless mercy…
biography: Helena Kowalska was born on 25 August 1905 at Głogowiec near Łódź, the third of ten children of a poor carpenter. After years as a domestic servant, she entered the Sisters of Our Lady of Mercy in Warsaw in 1925, taking the name Maria Faustina, and served as cook, gardener, and portress.

On 22 February 1931, in her cell at Płock, she saw the Lord, two rays issuing from his heart, and heard the command to paint his image signed 'Jesus, I trust in You' and to work for a feast of mercy on the Sunday after Easter. At Vilnius her confessor Michał Sopoćko arranged the first image, painted in 1934; the chaplet of Divine Mercy followed.

These revelations she recorded in her Diary, styling herself the secretary of Divine Mercy. She died of tuberculosis at Kraków on 5 October 1938, aged thirty-three. The Holy Office forbade the devotion for a time, lifting the ban in 1978.

Beatified in 1993, she was canonized by Pope John Paul II on 30 April 2000, and that day he proclaimed the Sunday after Easter Divine Mercy Sunday. She is venerated as patron of the Divine Mercy apostolate born of her revelations.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Maria Faustina Kowalska (vatican.va)
